# The Comics Code Authority

In the early 1950s, comics were blamed for juvenile delinquency, most famously in psychiatrist Fredric Wertham's 1954 book Seduction of the Innocent. The United States Senate held hearings on comics the same year.

In response, publishers created the Comics Code Authority in 1954. It was a self-regulating body, and comics that met its rules carried a seal on the cover. The rules banned graphic violence and horror, and required that crime never be shown in a positive way.

The code weakened over the following decades as publishers ignored or revised it. Marvel left it in 2001, and DC and Archie dropped it in 2011, which effectively ended it.
